senses.gloss: ch. sameto throw, swing; to put on; to impose.
units: <cite ref="Onkelos Exodus 15:1">Targ. Ex. XV, 1</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Ezekiel 16:5">Targ. Ez. XVI, 5</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on II Kings 18:14">Targ. II Kings XVIII, 14</cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 78:57">Targ. Ps. LXXVIII, 57</cite> (h. text <cite ref="T00811"><he>רְמִיָּה</he></cite>!); a. fr.—
<cite ref="Menachot 42a:13">Men. 42ᵃ</cite> <he>ר׳ חוטי</he> threw (attached) threads as show fringes; <he>ר׳ ארבע</he> put four threads on.
<cite ref="Shabbat 10a:2">Sabb. 10ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="Q00172"><he>פּוּזְמְקֵי</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Niddah 33b:18">Nidd. 33ᵇ</cite> <he>ר׳ ליה תורא</he> threw an ox down (slaughtered an ox) in his honor.
Men. 42ᵇ רְמִינָן להו ביורה we cast them into the boiler.—Part. pass. רְמֵי, רַמְיָא thrown down, lying.
<cite ref="Onkelos Deuteronomy 21:1">Targ. Deut. XXI, 1</cite> (O. ed. Vien. <cite ref="T00809"><he>רָמֵי</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Judges 19:27">Targ. Jud. XIX, 27</cite>; a. e.—
<cite ref="Zevachim 5a:2">Zeb. 5ᵃ</cite> <he>ר׳ ריש לקיש וכ׳</he> Resh Laḳish was lying on his belly in the college hall and asked &c.

Shebu. 34ᵇ כל מילתא דלא ר׳ עליה וכ׳ a thing which does not rest upon a man (in which he is not interested), he will do unconsciously; ib. 41ᵇ, sq.; B. Bath. 39ᵃ; a. fr.—ר׳ לבני [to put up bricks,] to make bricks.
<cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 11:3">Targ. Gen. XI, 3</cite>.
Targ. Ex. V, 7; a. e.—ר׳ תיגרא to create discord; to dispute.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 6:14">Targ. Prov. VI, 14</cite>; <cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 6:19">19</cite>; a. e.—
<cite ref="Shabbat 130a">Sabb. 130ᵃ</cite> <he>ליכא … דלא רָמוּ בה ת׳</he> there is no marriage contract at which the parties do not quarrel.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 10:2:20">Y. Snh. X, 29ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>בעי מִירְמִיתֵיה</he> wanted to lift it; a. e.

senses.gloss: [to pitch one thing against another,] to show an incongruity; to object. Nidd. l. c. ר׳ … מתניתין אהדדי pointed out an incongruity between two Mishnahs.
units: Taan. 4ᵇ גברא אגברא קא רָמִית thou provest an incongruity between two authorities (why can they not differ in opinion)? B. Mets. 22ᵇ רב פפא ר׳ כתיב וכ׳ Rab Papa raised an objection: it is written (Lev. XI, 38) ki yitten, and we read ki yuttan, how is this to be explained? Yeb. 108ᵇ ורְמִינְהִי וכ׳ and we shall show an incongruity in it, i.e. this disagrees with the Mishnah, &c.
<cite ref="Sukkah 16a:8">Succ. 16ᵃ</cite> <he>איכא דר׳ ליה מִירְמָא</he> some put it in the shape of pointing out a contradiction (between a Mishnah and a Boraitha); a. v. fr.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Judges 20:16">Targ. Jud. XX, 16</cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 1:14">Targ. Prov. I, 14</cite>; a. e.—
<cite ref="Shabbat 156b:3">Sabb. 156ᵇ</cite> <he>הוה מַרְמִינָן וכ׳</he> we used to cast our bread together (into one basket) and eat.
<cite ref="Shabbat 156b:3">Ib.</cite> <he>אנא קאים וארמינא</he> I will stand up and put the bread into the basket; a. e.
<cite ref="Pesachim 10b:6">Pes. 10ᵇ</cite> <he>אַרְמוּיֵי אַרְמֵיה מיניה</he> (not <he>ארמוייה</he>) it (the mouse) may have snatched it from the other mouse.
<cite ref="Chagigah 15b:2-4">Ḥag. 15ᵇ</cite> <he>אי … מאן מַרְמֵי ליה מאן</he> if I take him by the hand, who will tear him away from me? who?
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 34b:12">Ab. Zar. 34ᵇ</cite> <he>תַּרְמִינָךְ שעתך</he> (Ms. M. <he>תור מינך</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) may thy hour lift thee up (i.e. may thy luck be high)!
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Numbers 25:18">Targ. Y. Num. XXV, 18</cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 26:19">Targ. Prov. XXVI, 19</cite>.—
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 5">Lev. R. s. 5</cite> <he>הוה מְרַמֵּי במצוותה</he>, v. <cite ref="T00808">preced.</cite>; a. e.
<cite ref="Targum of I Chronicles 10:4">Targ. I Chr. X, 4</cite>, sq.

<cite ref="Chullin 13a:3">Ḥull. 13ᵃ</cite> <he>מקום … איתרמי ליה</he> (not <he>איתרמו</he>) because no suitable place (for slaughtering) offered itself there.
<cite ref="Shevuot 41b:11">Shebu. 41ᵇ</cite> <he>עד דמִתְרְמוּ בי תרי וכ׳</he> until two persons shall happen to come that have studied &c.; a. e.
